tools.name: get_bridge_status
tools.description: Requires sign-in. Return one of your bridge orders, including source confirmations, payout transaction hash, and any operator-review message.

tools.name: get_service_info
tools.description: Return supported chains, tokens, destination fees, limits, custody model, and documentation links. No sign-in required.

tools.name: list_my_bridges
tools.description: Requires sign-in. List the most recent bridge orders created by the signed-in wallet.

tools.name: login_finish
tools.description: Complete sign-in with the signature over the message from login_start. The MCP session is bound to this wallet; the bearer token stays server-side and is not returned.

tools.name: login_start
tools.description: Start a wallet sign-in and return the exact message the agent must sign with its own wallet. No private key is ever sent to the server.

tools.name: logout
tools.description: Forget the wallet in this MCP session. The wallet's on-chain funds are unaffected.

tools.name: prepare_deposit
tools.description: Requires sign-in. Validate a route, create a one-hour deposit intent, and return the exact token transfer to broadcast from the signed-in wallet. This does not move funds.

tools.name: quote_bridge
tools.description: Calculate the 1:1 conversion, fixed destination fee, and amount received for a route. Optionally validates a destination address. This does not create an order or move funds.

tools.name: submit_bridge
tools.description: Requires sign-in. Submit the source transaction hash for a prepared intent. The platform verifies the on-chain transfer and pays out automatically. The same intent and transaction hash are idempotent.

tools.name: validate_address
tools.description: Check whether an address is valid for an EVM, Solana, or Tron destination and return its canonical form.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Show which wallet is signed in to this MCP session.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "login_finish" references sensitive artifacts (bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_bridge_status · Private data: get_service_info, list_my_bridges, login_finish, login_start, logout, prepare_deposit, whoami · Public sink: prepare_deposit, submit_bridge.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_bridge_status · Private data: get_service_info, list_my_bridges, login_finish, login_start, logout, prepare_deposit, whoami · Public sink: prepare_deposit, submit_bridge

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
